newsitem.title: UK: Dollar holds footing above 1.75 marks in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dollar holds footing above 1.75 marks in Europe.

text.p: The dollar held its footing above 1.75 marks in afternoon Europe after jogging to fresh 40-month peaks against a shaky German unit.
"Breaking 1.75 marks was a tough nut to crack. We are above that level now and it should provide support," said a senior trader at a UK merchant bank.
Against the yen, the dollar was a touch weaker, still licking its wounds after an early battering following the flotation of the Thai baht, which prompted a flight into yen.
Markets were also in waiting mode ahead of the UK budget and the second-day of the Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting.
At 1410 GMT dollar/mark stood at 1.7510/20 against 1.7408/18 in late Europe on Tuesday, and just off fresh peaks of 1.7538 marks visited in afternoon Europe.
Dollar/yen was trading at 114.31 against 114.79/84 in late Europe but above its overnight low of 114.15.
The Federal Reserve began its last day of a two-day policy meeting at 9 a.m. (1300 GMT) on Wednesday and is slated to announce its decision at around 2:15 p.m (1815 GMT).
But despite a rosier outlook for the U.S. economy, the central bank is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged.
"Markets are sitting on their hands, waiting for the old Fed meeting to end and the UK budget to begin," said the trader.

The UK budget, the first by a Labour government since 1978, and keenly awaited by European markets, was originally scheduled for 1430 GMT but has been delayed by up to half-an-hour following allegations of a leak.

Sterling/mark, also said to have given dollar/mark a lift in Europe, steadied before the budget after coming within a whisker of Tuesday's five-year peak of 2.91 marks. Dlr/mark was also given a boost after German industrial production fell 0.2 percent in May, further dampening the outlook for the euro.

"We are seeing the dollar strengthen against the deutschemark as the softer euro stories continue to circulate. But the dollar isn't really striding ahead at the moment, and I don't think it will unless we get a surprise increase in rates after the Fed this afternoon," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International.
Against the yen, the dollar regained some composure after being sold off during Asian trade following the flotation of the Thai baht.

Overnight there was a rush to buy up the yen, which had gained something of a safe-haven status after the Bank of Thailand said it was dropping its pegged rates system against a basket of currencies and allowing the market to set exchange rates.

The Thai baht, meanwhile, had steadied after falling to a record low of 29.00 to the dollar in the offshore market on news of the float. It was at 28.800/300 at 1445 GMT against 24.25 just before the news.
